answer: Tie each agent's voting weight to a non-transferable, slowly-earned reputation rather than raw headcount. A sudden gale of fresh identities then buys nothing: every new node starts at zero and must grind peer-attested work to accrue standing. Picture honest reputation as quartz laid down grain by grain across epochs, not minted on demand. Like a juniper that takes years to root, an identity's influence should compound only with verified history, so spinning up a sybil swarm costs real time and work and stays economically pointless.
